suites.name: owasp-benchmark-python
suites.about: OWASP Benchmark for Python: each test case is a small Flask handler that is or is not really vulnerable to one CWE. Measures detection and false alarms.

suites.name: juice-shop
suites.about: OWASP Juice Shop (Node/Express/Angular): lines marked 'vuln-code-snippet vuln-line' are the known vulnerable lines of its coding challenges. Measures detection only; unmarked code is not labelled safe.

suites.name: securityeval
suites.about: SecurityEval: 121 insecure Python samples filed under the CWE they demonstrate. Measures detection only; every sample is vulnerable. Was held out until 2026-10-30, when its misses were used to add codewatch's crypto/TLS rules, and later its SSRF, regex and log injection rules. CWE-113 sonar_1/sonar_2 drove the Content-Type sinks of codewatch.python.web.xss (PLAN.md step 56).

suites.name: securityeval-copilot
suites.about: SecurityEval's Copilot-generated answers to the same prompts, each manually labelled vulnerable or safe. Held out: never used to write or tune codewatch rules. Measures detection and false alarms.

suites.name: securityeval-incoder
suites.about: SecurityEval's InCoder-generated answers to the same prompts, each manually labelled vulnerable or safe. Held out: never used to write or tune codewatch rules. Measures detection and false alarms.

suites.name: vulnerable-snippets-js
suites.about: Vulnerable-Code-Snippets: small vulnerable JS/TS examples filed by weakness. Held out: never used to write or tune codewatch rules. Measures detection only; every snippet is vulnerable.

suites.name: vulnerable-node-seeds
suites.about: vulnerable-node's SAST seeds: one known vulnerability per file plus clean controls that must stay quiet. Not held out: its first scan missed the SQL concatenation, NoSQL operator, prototype pollution and deserialization seeds and raised a false alarm on a clean control, which led to the JS guard sanitizer, SQL value-formatting and prototype-pollution rules. Measures detection and false alarms.

suites.name: cve-pairs-python
suites.about: Python CVE fix pairs. Reviewed GitHub advisories with exactly one fix commit that changes at most three non-test source files (120 lines or fewer) in web application code, i.e. request input reaching a sink in the project's own code rather than inside a framework or library. The commit before the fix is scanned for detection: a finding of the advisory's weakness near the changed lines, or one the fix makes go away. The fix commit is scanned for false alarms: such a finding that survives the fix or appears at it. Not held out: may be used to adjust rules (say so here when that happens). GHSA-9x43-5qcq-h79q (Grappelli) was used on 2026-10-31 to accept url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(url=...) as a redirect check; GHSA-f2mf-q878-gh58 (Parsl), GHSA-h6m6-jj8v-94jj (litellm) and GHSA-8whx-v8qq-pq64 (changedetection.io) to add Flask route and FastAPI text parameters as request sources, pandas and Prisma raw-SQL sinks, and typed Flask converters; GHSA-6rmf-cv6p-4h27 (django-termsandconditions) and GHSA-g3cm-qg2v-2hj5 (pyLoad), at their fix commits, to add values used inside a passing is_safe/is_valid-style check, request.url_root/host_url as redirect bases, and calls to project functions that can't return a parameter as clean (this loses GHSA-g3cm's vulnerable commit, whose flaw is its own is_safe_url). Cases added 2026-11-02 were chosen from GitHub's reviewed pip advisories since 2021 (CWE 22, 79, 89, 94, 502, 601, 611, 78, 918, 1336) by fix size, then read one by one; the decisions and reasons are in PLAN.md step 22. On 2026-11-02 (PLAN.md step 22, first round) GHSA-527m-2xhr-j27g, GHSA-wc6j-5g83-xfm6, GHSA-48rp-jc79-2264 and GHSA-vwhf-3v6x-wff8 at their fixes were used to accept raising validators named for what they check, base + os.sep prefix checks on resolved paths, Flask make_response of a dict or list, and lookups through a store; GHSA-h454-rq3m-89rc (Django URL arguments), GHSA-9jj8-v89v-xjvw (route parameters tainted where declared, name-only re.sub), GHSA-r25m-cr6v-p9hq (FileResponse, sanitise_ names) and GHSA-g53g-q539-93cv (requests url=) to add sources and sinks. Cases added 2026-11-02 in a second batch (PLAN.md step 23) follow the same rule, read from OSV's export of GitHub's reviewed PyPI advisories (GitHub's advisory API was not reachable from the session), with three pre-2021 advisories added under the same size rule (two here, one blind); decisions and reasons are in benchmarks/cve-candidates-2026-11-02.tsv. None of them has been used to write or adjust rules. Cases added 2026-11-02 in a third batch (PLAN.md step 24) widen that rule: CWE 23, 36, 73, 77, 90, 113, 643, 943 and 1333 as well, fixes of up to five non-test source files and 200 lines when the flow is still clear, Quart, Starlette and Flask-RESTful/Flask-AppBuilder apps counted as Flask/FastAPI, and pre-2021 advisories; decisions are in benchmarks/cve-candidates-2026-11-02-batch3.tsv. None of them has been used to write or adjust rules. Cases added 2026-11-03 in a fourth batch (PLAN.md step 27) follow the third batch's rule, read from OSV's export of GitHub's reviewed PyPI advisories: one open case (Arches GHSA-gmpq, 147 changed lines ignoring re-indented SQL, within step 24's widened limits; Modoboa GHSA-wwv8 was rejected at review for touching 10 files) and three blind in cve-pairs-blind-python-5; decisions and reasons are in benchmarks/cve-candidates-2026-11-03.tsv. None used for rules yet. Cases added 2026-11-03 from GitHub's unreviewed advisories (Python web apps not on PyPI; research by a separate agent per AGENTS.md, reviewed here, PLAN.md step 30): 6 open, 5 blind in cve-pairs-blind-python-6 here; decisions in benchmarks/cve-candidates-2026-11-03-python-unreviewed.tsv. None used for rules yet. Cases added 2026-11-03 from the second batch of unreviewed advisories (PLAN.md step 30): agent-zero GHSA-8j45 and pyLoad GHSA-3mmf here, 3 blind in cve-pairs-blind-python-7; decisions in benchmarks/cve-candidates-2026-11-03-python-unreviewed-2.tsv. None used for rules yet. On 2026-11-04 GHSA-3864-rp2m-2qfj (libre-chat) and GHSA-v9w6-9hq9-33ch (LightRAG) were used to make a FastAPI route's UploadFile parameters (and lists of them) a source through their .filename, and LightRAG to rewrite match statements whose case patterns span lines. Also on 2026-11-04: pgAdmin GHSA-v395-x24j-4r3g to make its driver's execute_scalar/execute_dict/execute_2darray/execute_void SQL sinks; GHSA-cr8c-972v-rmp3 to make req.form/args/values/files/get_json() a source, to stop a Path built for a relative_to() check being a sink, and to accept a normalised path's relative_to() in a try that returns on ValueError as a containment check; GHSA-7r93-vp6c-cw5m to accept a named safe-URL check that replaces the value (unless an `and` can skip it) and Flask-Login's login_url() as an internal URL; psiturk GHSA-9mq4-9556-6qxq to stop a key-presence check on request.args clearing the whole request. GHSA-fghj-qqgj-7rxf (SQLBot, added 2026-11-04) was used the same day to accept os.path.commonpath() containment checks; its scope was widened to include its request model. GHSA-2689 (Whoogle) is filed as CWE-78, but its fix replaces pickle with json for the preferences cookie: CWE-502 added on 2026-11-05 (PLAN.md step 43), with no rule changed.

suites.about: CVE fix pairs in the templates and front-end JavaScript of Python web apps (Django, Flask, FastAPI): the fix changes a template or a script the app ships. Chosen and scored like cve-pairs-python, with templates (.html, Jinja) and JS/TS counted as source. Not held out: may be used to adjust rules (say so here when that happens). Cases added 2026-11-02 were chosen from GitHub's reviewed pip advisories since 2021 (CWE 22, 79, 89, 94, 502, 601, 611, 78, 918, 1336) by fix size, then read one by one; the decisions and reasons are in PLAN.md step 22. On 2026-11-02 GHSA-mxvc-fwgx-j778 (Whoogle) was used to add request data passed to a template variable printed with |safe as an XSS sink. On 2026-11-02 (second batch, a cloud session) 21 more cases were added from the same advisories, widened to all years, to fixes over three files or 120 lines when every change is the same weakness, and to advisories whose extra commits are backports of one fix (the main-branch commit is used); none used for rules yet. Decisions and reasons: PLAN.md step 22. On 2026-11-03 the Flask extension-based autoescape model was added for GHSA-pwgc-w4x9-gw67 (changedetection.io): .jinja/.jinja2/.j2 templates are not autoescaped by Flask, so the template rule treats their variables as unescaped for render_template/flask.render_template calls, a new hotspot codewatch.templates.not-autoescaped reports them for stored data, and .jinja/.jinja2/.j2/.djhtml are now scanned as templates. Test: test_flask_jinja_templates_are_not_autoescaped. The nightly run measures the suite. Cases added 2026-11-03 from GitHub's unreviewed advisories (Python web apps not on PyPI; research by a separate agent per AGENTS.md, reviewed here, PLAN.md step 30): 1 (Formspree GHSA-2wvm, a template-only fix) here; decisions in benchmarks/cve-candidates-2026-11-03-python-unreviewed.tsv. None used for rules yet. Cases added 2026-11-03 from the second batch of unreviewed advisories (PLAN.md step 30): bird-lg GHSA-xjrp here, 1 blind in cve-pairs-blind-python-frontend-3; decisions in benchmarks/cve-candidates-2026-11-03-python-unreviewed-2.tsv. None used for rules yet. GHSA-2wvm-9j4x-757c (Formspree) was used on 2026-11-04 to add codewatch.templates.request-in-url-attribute (request query or form values printed at the start of an href/src/action, or inside an event handler). On 2026-11-07 (PLAN.md step 52) Modoboa GHSA-c467 and calibre-web GHSA-wrp6 were used to make form field values ($(...).val(), getElementById/querySelector(...).value) a source of codewatch.js.xss, a $-named jQuery variable's .html()/.append() a sink, htmlEncode-style functions a sanitizer, and to stop a date in a file's opening comment marking it as a vendored library.

cases.summary: The MASTER_PASSWORD_HOOK setting, introduced in pgAdmin 4 7.2, lets an administrator configure an external command that returns a per-user encryption key, with %u in the configured string replaced by the current user's name. The previous implementation substituted the username directly into the command string and executed the result with subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True). Because the username can originate from an external authentication source (OAuth/OIDC claims, Kerberos, webserver auth) rather than a value pgAdmin fully controls, a username containing shell metacharacters (';', '$()', backticks, pipes, '&&', newlines) allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary commands as the pgAdmin service account in any deployment where the configured hook string uses %u.
